previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for evaluation of right-sided chest pain with palpitations and worsening chronic abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She had uncontrolled type 1 diabetes due to loss of her glucometer and missed insulin doses. Initial workup ruled out myocardial infarction with normal EKGs and troponins. She accidentally dislodged her GJ tube during the admission, requiring temporary Foley placement and subsequent replacement by interventional radiology. A low-grade fever and erythema at the tube site led to a short course of clindamycin, with improvement. Pain was managed with IV Dilaudid and a structured regimen allowing one patient-chosen extra dose daily. Insulin was adjusted with endocrinology input, resulting in a new regimen of 60 units Lantus at bedtime and a sliding scale for Humalog. She improved clinically, maintained oral intake, and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete antibiotics, follow up with her providers, and manage her diabetes and pain medications appropriately.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___.  

Comparison is made with a prior study from ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Sharp scapular pain with inspiration, question pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  PA and lateral views of the chest were obtained.  Low lung volumes
limit evaluation.  A Port-A-Cath is again noted overlying the right chest wall
with catheter tip in the expected location of the superior vena cava. 
Allowing for low lung volumes, the lungs are clear bilaterally.  There is no
pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal. 
Bony structures are intact.  Clips in the right upper quadrant are noted.  A
catheter is also noted in the upper abdomen.

IMPRESSION:  Limited study without definite signs of pneumonia or CHF.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with ___ tube placed on ___, possibly
displaced, to evaluate/reposition the same.

COMPARISON:  Perc G/G-J tube placement ___.

RADIOLOGIST: ___ and ___. The attending ___
___ reviewed the procedure.

The risks and benefits of the procedure were explained to the patient. Written
informed consent was obtained.  The patient was brought to the angiography
suite and placed supine on the table.  Her abdomen and the indwelling ___ tube
were prepped and draped in standard sterile fashion.  A preprocedure timeout
was performed per standard ___ protocol. The patient strongly feels that the
existing MIC ___ tube be exchanged for ___ tube which she had
previously.

An initial scout view of the abdomen demonstrated a ___ MIC
gastrojejunostomy tube in standard position with the tip terminating in the
jejunum with the inflated balloon positioned in the stomach.  The catheter tip
position in the jejunum was confirmed by injecting contrast.  Following this a
___ wire was advanced through the tube and then the catheter was removed
over the wire.  A Kumpe catheter was placed and the ___ wire was exchanged
for an Amplatz wire.  The Kumpe catheter was then removed and a ___
___ gastrojejunostomy tube was placed over the wire.  The wire was then
removed and a pigtail was formed in the duodenal bulb.  Contrast was injected
demonstrating good opacification of the jejunum.  Pigtail was locked and
catheter secured to the skin with StatLock and capped.  The catheter can be
used immediately.  There were no immediate complications.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of gastrojejunal tube malposition.
2.  Successful exchange of a ___ ___ gastrojejunal tube over a
preexisting ___ MIC gastrojejunal tube.
